MINUTES OF THE SPECIAL MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  September 8, 2025

Vice Chair Rosoff called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers,
Norwalk City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll
call were Chair LeGaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner
Hoskins, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez and Commissioner Greenidge. Also, present was
Rita Ruiz, Interim Director, Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst, Marissa Velez, Office
Assistant II, Rudy Garcia, Public Safety Lieutenant and the Drone Team.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Apodaca motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on August 4, 2025. Commissioner Dr.
Rodriguez seconded the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Vice Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins,
  Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, and Commissioner Fernandez-Silva
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Greenidge
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

Officer Commendation Rafael Andrade

Mrs. Lomas introduced Public Safety Lt. Rudy Garcia, who presented a commendation
to PSO Rafael Andrade. On August 15, PSO Andrade recovered a loaded handgun near
Studebaker Rd. and Excelsior Dr., securing it until LASD took over. His swift response
prevented a potential public safety threat and highlighted his commitment to the
community.

Drone Presentation

Interim Director Rita Ruiz introduced Public Safety Lt. Rudy Garcia, who provided an
update on the Drone Program. Since the first drone was purchased in 2019, three more
have been added. Lt. Garcia, a certified pilot since 2019, oversees training and ensures
FAA compliance.
 Training Requirements

Lt. Rudy Garcia provided an overview of the department's efforts to ensure FAA
compliance within the Drone Program. All drone pilots are required to maintain FAA
certification, which includes ongoing training and meeting operational requirements
established by the Federal Aviation Administration. The department currently has four
certified pilots and four pilots-in-training, all actively engaged in hands-on training and
compliance with FAA guidelines for safe and legal drone operations. This includes
adherence to flight regulations, airspace restrictions, and reporting practices to ensure
the safety of both operators and the public. The Drone Program team members are:

  •  Lt. R. Garcia – Certified Pilot
  •  Sgt. J. Gomez – Certified Pilot
  •  PSO Y. Gomez – Certified Pilot
  •  PSO A. Contreras – Certified Pilot
  •  PSO R. Sanchez – Certified Pilot
  •  Sgt. J. Warren – Pilot Trainee
  •  PSO R. Andrade – Pilot Trainee
  •  PSO N. Cuadras – Pilot Trainee
  •  PSO A. Wood – Pilot Trainee

Drone Deployment-Recent Events/Highlights:

Lt. Rudy Garcia reported that the Drone Program has been actively used at recent
community events, including the Halloween Parade, 4th of July Fireworks Show,
Summer Concert Series, and Easter Egg Hunt. Drones provided aerial support for
crowd monitoring, situational awareness, and coordination with event staff, proving to
be a valuable tool for enhancing public safety and response during large gatherings.

Wendy’s Interactive Event
Lt. Garcia highlighted a recent drone deployment at the Wendy’s interactive community
event, where heavy traffic created safety and congestion concerns. The drone provided
real-time aerial monitoring, enabling field units to coordinate with traffic control, ease
congestion, and keep vehicles moving efficiently. This proactive use of drone technology
minimized delays, addressed motorist concerns, and enhanced the overall event
experience.

CYA Property Aerial Patrol

On July 17, 2025, the Drone Team conducted an aerial patrol of the former CYA facility,
recently turned over to the city. The patrol was initiated in response to reports of
vandalism, trespassing, and theft. Operators observed three trespassers, who were
contacted by field personnel and advised of the violation. The drone’s proactive use
enhanced site security enabled a quick response and helped deter further incidents.
 The Commission then viewed a video highlighting recent special events and monthly
activities.

Lastly, the Commission discussed the development of a mission and vision statement for
the Public Safety Commission, along with establishing minimum requirements and duties
for commissioners. Input is being sought from each commissioner regarding what should
be included. This discussion will continue through commission roundtable and email
correspondence with Chair Legaspi, Vice Chair Rosoff, and Commissioner Greenidge.

STAFF COMMENTS

Interim Director Rita Ruiz reported that the Commission’s draft mission and vision
statements, along with recommendations, have been compiled based on prior feedback.
Mrs. Lomas will follow up after the meeting with the draft for review and further input.

Policy, Procedure, and Commissioner Duties:

  •  Promote public awareness of security and safety in Norwalk.
  •  Provide educational opportunities to foster protective concern and community
  awareness.
  •  Hear and decide matters related to disabled person’s parking zones in the public
  right-of-way.
  •  Respond to security and public safety hazards, preparing fact-finding reports and
  recommendations.
  •  Recommend adoption, amendment, or repeal of ordinances or resolutions
  affecting public safety and municipal parking codes, after public input.
  •  Acquire information through professional seminars or workshops as needed.
  •  The Commission does not serve as a review board for the Sheriff’s Department
  or its personnel.

Vision Statement:

The Public Safety Commission is dedicated to fostering a safe, informed, and engaged
community by partnering with residents, City leaders, and Public Safety Officers. The
Commission is committed to transparency, ethical conduct, and professional
representation.

Mission Statement:

  •  Educate and involve residents in understanding Public Safety and the Los
  Angeles Sheriff’s Department.
  •  Support law enforcement and City initiatives through participation in events,
  outreach programs, and public engagement.
  •  Uphold accountability and professionalism through consistent attendance, ethical
  training, and visible representation at City meetings and events.
   •  Serve with dedication, loyalty, and honesty to strengthen trust between the City,
  Public Safety personnel, and the community.
  •  Strive to be visible, approachable, and committed partners in ensuring the well-
  being of Norwalk and its residents.

Mrs. Lomas reviewed the 2025 Monthly Calendar and highlighted September as
National Emergency Awareness Month. Interim Director Ruiz shared that the
department launched a “What’s in Your Go Bag?” contest on social media to engage
residents and offer a chance to win a prize.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS
Vice Chair Rosoff thanked Lt. Garcia, the drone pilots, and trainees for their efforts and
commitment to community safety.

Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez inquired about qualifications to oversee the Drone Program.
Lt. Garcia noted he has been a certified drone pilot since 2019, has over 21 years with
the Public Safety Department, and is pursuing a Bachelor of Science in Autonomous and
Drone Systems at Fullerton State to further enhance his expertise.

Commissioner Fernandez-Silva asked about calls for service at the former CYA property.
Lt. Garcia explained the city recently acquired the site, and Public Safety now provides
security oversight, responding to related service calls.

Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez emphasized the importance of officer presence in the field
and asked if the department is tracking monthly trends or data patterns. Interim Director
Rita Ruiz advised this topic to be addressed at the next meeting and invited
commissioners to suggest items for inclusion in the monthly activity report.

Commissioner Apodaca asked which events staff preferred the Commissioners to attend
to meet participation requirements. Interim Director Ruiz suggested options including
Cadet Meetings, Senior Center Meetings, Business Watch Meetings, and Neighborhood
Watch Meetings. She noted cadet meetings feature guest speakers and would benefit
from mentorship, with a suggested format for a 20-minute presentation followed by Q&A.
Events are typically held at City facilities, such as the recent meeting at the Sports
Complex.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:

Andrew expressed concern regarding recent immigration activities and raids occurring in
communities following the Supreme Court’s decision to overturn a temporary prison order.
He noted fears of armed individuals impersonating federal agents and the potential risks
this poses to residents. Andrew acknowledged the City’s existing communication tools,
such as safety alerts, and suggested exploring how similar systems could be used to keep
residents informed of unlawful activity and enhance community safety. He urged the
Commission to take a proactive approach to protect residents.
 ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:43 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
